style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: The cosmic roll-call. Two summonses, one from the heavens and one from the earth, and between them every category of created thing is called by name to praise the LORD. Angels and armies, sun, moon, and stars, the highest heavens and the waters above the sky -- praise Him, because He commanded and they were created, and He fixed them by a decree they do not transgress. Then from below: sea monsters and ocean deeps, fire, hail, snow, mist, and storm wind doing His word; mountains and hills, orchards and cedars, wild beasts and cattle, crawling things and birds; and only then humanity, by rank -- kings, peoples, princes, judges -- and by age, young men and young women, old and small. The reason for the second half matches the first: His name alone is exalted, His majesty above earth and heaven. And the last verse narrows the whole universe to one point: He has raised up a horn for His people, Israel, the people near to Him. The stars praise Him from where He placed them; His saints praise Him from beside Him. Francis of Assisi's Canticle of the Sun is this psalm's child, sung in Umbrian.

1.text: Praise the LORD! Praise the LORD from up in the heavens; praise Him, all you in the heights!
1.amp: Praise ye the LORD [halelu-Yah]. Praise [halal] ye the LORD [YHWH] from the heavens [shamayim]: praise Him in the heights [marom].
1.notes: The cosmic roll-call opens at the top: min ha-shamayim, ba-meromim (H8064, H4791). Verses 1-6 summon the upper creation, 7-14 the lower; halal (H1984) is the verb for both, and every named thing is a choir section.

2.text: Praise Him, every one of His angels; praise Him, all His heavenly armies!
2.amp: Praise [halal] ye Him, all His angels [malak -- messengers]: praise ye Him, all His hosts [tsaba -- armies].
2.notes: kol malakhav, kol tsebaav (H4397, H6635): the messengers and the armies of heaven -- Isaiah's seraphim and the multitude of Luke 2:13, ordered to their own business. The higher the creature, the more praise is its native language.

3.text: Praise Him, O sun and moon; praise Him, every shining star!
3.amp: Praise [halal] ye Him, sun [shemesh] and moon [yareach]: praise Him, all ye stars [kokab] of light [or].
3.notes: shemesh, yareach, kokhbe or (H8121, H3394, H3556, H216): the lights Genesis 1:16 pointedly refused to name, lest they be worshiped -- here named and told to worship. The pagan gods demoted to choir members.

4.text: Praise Him, you heavens beyond the heavens, and you waters stored up above the sky!
4.amp: Praise [halal] Him, ye heavens [shamayim] of heavens, and ye waters [mayim] that be above the heavens.
4.notes: sheme ha-shamayim (H8064), the heavens' heavens -- the outermost tier -- and the mayim (H4325) above the firmament of Genesis 1:7, the storehouses of rain. Even the reservoirs behind the sky have a part to sing.

5.text: Let them all praise the name of the LORD, for He gave the command, and they came into being.
5.amp: Let them praise [halal] the name [shem] of the LORD [YHWH]: for He commanded [tsavah], and they were created [bara].
5.notes: The upper choir's reason: hu tsivvah ve-nibrau (H6680, H1254) -- He gave the order and they came into being. bara is Genesis 1:1's verb, God's alone: things that owe their existence to a command owe their praise to the Commander.

6.text: He set them in place forever and ever; He gave a decree that will not pass away.
6.amp: He has also established [amad -- made stand] them for ever [ad] and ever [olam]: He has made [natan] a decree [choq] which shall not pass [abar].
6.notes: amad la-ad le-olam (H5975, H5703, H5769): the heavenly bodies stationed permanently -- and choq natan ve-lo yaabor (H2706, H5414, H5674), a statute the stars do not transgress. Creation's obedience is the model; verse 14's people are the ones who needed the statute repeated.

7.text: Praise the LORD from the earth, you great sea creatures and all the ocean depths;
7.amp: Praise [halal] the LORD [YHWH] from the earth [eretz], ye dragons [tannin -- sea monsters] and all deeps [tehom -- the abyss]:
7.notes: The second half starts at the bottom: min ha-eretz (H776), and first the tanninim and kol tehomot (H8577, H8415) -- the sea monsters and the primeval deeps, the chaos-symbols of pagan myth, here first in line for the earthly choir. Nothing is too wild to praise.

8.text: fire and hail, snow and mist, storm wind carrying out His word;
8.amp: Fire [esh], and hail [barad]; snow [sheleg], and vapour [qitor -- smoke, mist]; stormy [saar] wind [ruach] fulfilling [asah -- doing] His word [dabar]:
8.notes: esh, barad, sheleg, qitor (H784, H1259, H7950, H7008) -- the violent and the vaporous -- and ruach searah osah debaro (H7307, H5591, H6213, H1697): the tempest as an obedient servant executing orders. Weather praises by compliance (cf. Psalm 147:15-18).

9.text: you mountains and every hill, you fruit trees and every cedar;
9.amp: Mountains [har], and all hills [gibah]; fruitful [peri] trees [ets], and all cedars [erez]:
9.notes: harim, gebaot (H2022, H1389); ets peri and kol arazim (H6086, H6529, H730) -- the cultivated orchard and the wild Lebanon cedar side by side. Landscape and forest are choir sections, not scenery.

10.text: wild animals and all livestock, creeping things and birds on the wing;
10.amp: Beasts [chayyah -- wild animals], and all cattle [behemah]; creeping things [remes], and flying fowl ['birds of wing', tsippor kanaph, the KJV margin]:
10.notes: chayyah and behemah (H2416, H929), wild and tame; remes (H7431) and tsippor kanaph (H6833, H3671) -- the crawlers and the winged. Genesis 1's sixth- and fifth-day categories, reassembled for worship.

11.text: you kings of the earth and every people, you princes and every judge on earth;
11.amp: Kings [melek] of the earth [eretz], and all people [leom]; princes [sar], and all judges [shaphat] of the earth:
11.notes: Humanity enters late and by rank: malkhe eretz, leummim, sarim, shophete eretz (H4428, H3816, H8269, H8199). The powers are summoned after the cattle -- precedence in the cosmic choir runs by creation order, not by throne.

12.text: young men and young women too, old men together with children --
12.amp: Both young men [bachur], and maidens [betulah]; old men [zaqen], and children [naar]:
12.notes: bachurim, betulot, zeqenim, nearim (H970, H1330, H2205, H5288): every age and both sexes -- Joel 2:28's demographic, the whole human span with no exempt category. The oldest and the smallest sing the same word.

13.text: let them all praise the name of the LORD, for His name alone is lifted high beyond reach; His majesty towers over earth and heaven.
13.amp: Let them praise [halal] the name [shem] of the LORD [YHWH]: for His name alone is excellent ['exalted', sagab, the KJV margin -- high beyond reach]; His glory [hod -- majesty] is above the earth [eretz] and heaven [shamayim].
13.notes: The lower choir's reason, matching verse 5: nisgab shemo levaddo (H7682, H8034) -- His name alone is set high and out of reach -- and hodo (H1935) above eretz AND shamayim, the two halves of the psalm. The whole roll-call converges on one Name.

14.text: And He has raised up a horn for His people -- praise for all His faithful ones, for the children of Israel, the people near to Him. Praise the LORD!
14.amp: He also exalts [rum] the horn [qeren -- strength, dignity] of His people [am], the praise [tehillah] of all His saints [chasid -- covenant-faithful ones]; even of the children [ben] of Israel [Yisrael], a people [am] near [qarov] unto Him. Praise ye the LORD [halelu-Yah].
14.notes: After the cosmos, the smallest section gets the last verse: va-yarem qeren le-ammo (H7311, H7161, H5971) -- the horn raised, the symbol of restored strength Zechariah takes up in the Benedictus (cf. Luke 1:69) -- and am qerovo (H7138), the people NEAR Him. Stars obey Him from a distance; Israel is the choir He stands among.
